examples.ko: 올여름에는 비가 안 와서 땅이 가물었어요.
examples.en: It did not rain this summer, so the ground has been dry.
If there is a long dry spell, the crops dry up.

examples.ko: 가문 논에 물을 대느라 하루 종일 바빴어요.
examples.en: I was busy all day bringing water to the parched rice field.
Every year around this time it is dry, and I worry.

examples.ko: 너무 가물지 않으면 좋겠다고 농부가 말했어요.
examples.en: The farmer said he hopes it will not be too dry.

examples.ko: 몇 달째 가물어서 저수지 물이 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: It has been dry for months, so the reservoir has shrunk a lot.

explain: 비가 오랫동안 오지 않아 땅이나 날씨가 메마를 때 써요. 'ㄹ' 받침이라서 '가문 땅'처럼 'ㄴ' 앞에서 'ㄹ'이 빠져요. 명사형은 '가뭄'이고, 눈이나 기억이 흐릿한 '가물가물'과는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used when it has not rained for a long time and the ground or weather turns dry. Because the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops before ㄴ, as in '가문 땅'. The noun is '가뭄', and it is a different word from '가물가물', which means hazy.

examples.en: We set out early to see the sunset at the West Sea.
People gathered to take photos of the sunset.
This island is famous for its beautiful sunset.
The sky stained by the sunset was really pretty.
We went up to the observatory in time for the sunset.
The scenery of the setting sun stays in your memory for a long time.

explain: 관광 안내나 글에서 많이 보이는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '노을'이나 '해 질 녘'이라고 하고, 해가 지는 일 자체는 '일몰'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This word appears often in tourist guides and writing. In daily conversation people say '노을' or '해 질 녘', and '일몰' refers to the sun setting itself.

examples.en: The morning sunlight shines down through the window.
Moonlight was shining down on the lake.

examples.ko: 나무 사이로 햇빛이 내리비치는 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked along a path where sunlight shone down through the trees.
When the midsummer sun shines down, the ground gets hot.

examples.ko: 가로등 불빛이 골목에 내리비쳐서 무섭지 않았어요.
examples.en: Streetlight shone down on the alley, so I wasn't scared.
When the clouds cleared, sunlight shone down brightly.

explain: 위에서 아래로 비추는 빛에 쓰고, 햇빛뿐 아니라 달빛이나 불빛에도 어울려요. 햇볕이 뜨겁게 쏟아질 때는 '내리쬐다'가 더 잘 어울려요. 활용은 '내리비쳐요', '내리비쳤어요'예요.
explain_en: It describes light shining from above to below, and fits moonlight and lamplight as well as sunlight. When the sun beats down hotly, '내리쬐다' fits better. The conjugations are '내리비쳐요' and '내리비쳤어요'.

en: strong; highly likely (of a possibility); rich

examples.ko: 이번 사고는 사람의 실수일 가능성이 농후해요.
examples.en: It is highly likely that this accident was human error.

examples.ko: 그 후보가 이길 가능성이 농후하다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying that candidate is very likely to win.

examples.ko: 이 글에는 개인적인 감정이 농후하게 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: This writing is full of strong personal feeling.

examples.ko: 범인이 가까운 사람일 혐의가 농후해 보여요.
examples.en: It looks very likely that the culprit is someone close.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 코미디 색채가 농후해서 편하게 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: This movie has a strong comedy flavor, so you can watch it easily.

examples.ko: 올해 경기가 나빠질 우려가 농후한 상황이에요.
examples.en: It's a situation where the economy is very likely to worsen this year.

explain: 주로 '가능성이 농후하다', '혐의가 농후하다', '우려가 농후하다'처럼 어떤 일이나 경향이 강할 때 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '가능성이 높다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is mainly used in phrases like '가능성이 농후하다' (very likely), '혐의가 농후하다' and '우려가 농후하다' when something or a tendency is strong. It is common in news and writing, while in everyday talk '가능성이 높다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: There is a halo around the moon in the night sky tonight.

examples.ko: 달무리가 지면 다음 날 비가 온다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a saying that if the moon has a halo, it rains the next day.
I looked at the halo around the moon outside the window for a long time.
On a night with a halo around the moon, even the wind is gentle.
When I took a photo, the halo around the moon came out big.

examples.ko: 할머니는 달무리를 보고 내일 날씨를 맞히셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother looked at the moon's halo and guessed tomorrow's weather correctly.

explain: 달에 무리(둥근 빛 테두리)가 생기는 현상이고, '달무리가 지다/끼다'처럼 말해요. 해에 생기는 것은 '햇무리'라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is the ring of light that forms around the moon, and people say '달무리가 지다/끼다'. The same thing around the sun is called '햇무리', so it helps to learn them as a pair.

examples.ko: 갑자기 한파가 몰아닥쳐서 모두 두꺼운 옷을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: A cold wave suddenly hit, so everyone took out thick clothes.

examples.ko: 태풍이 몰아닥치기 전에 창문을 단단히 닫았어요.
examples.en: I shut the windows tightly before the typhoon hit.
At the end of the year, work comes crashing in all at once.

examples.ko: 경제 위기가 몰아닥친 뒤 가게가 많이 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: After the economic crisis hit, many stores closed.

examples.ko: 불행이 한꺼번에 몰아닥칠 때는 누구나 힘들어요.
examples.en: Anyone has a hard time when misfortunes pile on all at once.
Even though a downpour struck, I went to the meeting place.

explain: 추위, 태풍, 위기, 일 같은 것이 갑자기 세게, 한꺼번에 밀려올 때 써요. 그냥 '오다'보다 감당하기 힘든 느낌이 있고, 보통 좋지 않은 일에 써요. 비바람이 세게 부는 모습에는 '몰아치다'도 써요.
explain_en: It describes cold, storms, crises or work suddenly rushing in hard and all at once. It feels more overwhelming than a plain '오다' and is normally used for unpleasant things. For strong wind and rain, '몰아치다' is also used.

en: come into one's prime; hit one's stride

examples.ko: 요즘 그 배우의 연기가 한창 물올랐어요.
examples.en: That actor's acting is at its peak these days.
When spring comes, sap rises in every branch.
With his peak skills, he won the competition.
As the weather warms up, the willow trees start to come alive too.

examples.ko: 한창 물오른 선수라서 다음 경기도 기대돼요.
examples.en: He is a player in top form, so I'm looking forward to the next game too.

examples.ko: 요즘 글솜씨가 물올라서 글이 잘 써져요.
examples.en: My writing has hit its stride lately, so the words come easily.

explain: 나무에 물이 올라 싱싱해지는 모습에서, 사람의 연기·실력·인기가 한창 좋아질 때도 써요. '물오른 연기', '물오른 실력'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. '오르다'가 르 불규칙이라 '물올라요, 물올랐어요'로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It describes a tree getting fresh as sap rises, and it is also used when a person's acting, skill or popularity is at its best. It often appears as '물오른 연기' or '물오른 실력'. Because '오르다' is a 르-irregular verb, it becomes '물올라요' and '물올랐어요'.

examples.en: A trace amount of heavy metals was detected in this water.
Even a tiny amount of salt changes the taste.

examples.ko: 이 약에는 카페인이 미량 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine contains a trace of caffeine.

examples.ko: 미량이라도 매일 먹으면 몸에 쌓일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a tiny amount can build up in your body if you eat it every day.

examples.ko: 검사 결과 미량이 나왔지만 걱정할 수준은 아니래요.
examples.en: A trace amount showed up in the test, but they say it's nothing to worry about.
They said it's fine because it's a tiny amount, not a large one.

explain: '조금'이나 '약간'과 달리 눈으로 보기 힘들 만큼 아주 적은 양에 써요. 성분 검사, 뉴스, 설명문에서 '미량의 ~'로 자주 나오고, 반대말은 '다량'이에요.
explain_en: Unlike '조금' or '약간', it is used for an amount so small you can hardly see it. It often appears in test results, news and explanatory writing as '미량의 ~', and its opposite is '다량' (a large amount).

examples.en: Firefly lights glimmered on a country summer night.
The children ran off to see the firefly lights.

examples.ko: 반딧불은 깨끗한 곳에서만 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see firefly lights only in clean places.
Small lights came on one by one like fireflies.
I went to Muju to see the firefly festival.
Dozens of firefly lights blink in the forest.

explain: 반딧불은 반딧불이가 내는 빛이고, 곤충은 '반딧불이'라고 해요. 둘의 소리가 거의 같아서 문장에서 구분해 들어야 해요. 옛날에는 '개똥벌레'라고도 했어요.
explain_en: 반딧불 is the light a firefly makes, while the insect itself is 반딧불이. The two sound almost the same, so you must tell them apart in context. Long ago the insect was also called 개똥벌레.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 곳에 두면 알이 일주일 뒤에 부화해요.
examples.en: If you keep the egg somewhere warm, it hatches after a week.
I took a photo of a chick hatching.

examples.ko: 거북이 알이 부화하면 새끼들이 바다로 가요.
examples.en: When the turtle eggs hatch, the baby turtles head for the sea.
This egg hasn't hatched yet.

examples.ko: 알이 부화한 뒤 어미 새가 먹이를 가져다줘요.
examples.en: After the eggs hatch, the mother bird brings food.
Frog eggs hatch and become tadpoles.

explain: 보통 '알이 부화하다'처럼 알을 주어로 쓰지만 '병아리가 부화하다'라고도 말해요. 사람이 일부러 알을 깨어나게 할 때는 '부화시키다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is usually used with the egg as the subject, as in '알이 부화하다', though '병아리가 부화하다' is also said. When a person deliberately gets eggs to hatch, '부화시키다' is used.

examples.en: I found the Big Dipper in the clear night sky.
The Big Dipper is shaped like a ladle.

examples.ko: 아빠가 북두칠성으로 북극성 찾는 법을 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My dad showed me how to find the North Star using the Big Dipper.
In the countryside, the Big Dipper is clearly visible.

examples.ko: 북두칠성의 일곱 별을 하나씩 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: I counted the seven stars of the Big Dipper one by one.
It is hard to see the Big Dipper in the city.

explain: 국자 모양으로 늘어선 일곱 별이에요. 국자 끝의 두 별을 이어 길게 늘이면 북극성을 찾을 수 있어요. 전통적으로 수명을 맡은 별로 여겨서, 관 바닥에 까는 '칠성판'에도 일곱 별 모양으로 구멍을 냈어요. 줄여서 '칠성'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the seven stars arranged in the shape of a ladle. If you extend a line through the two stars at the end of the ladle, you can find the North Star. Traditionally the stars were believed to govern lifespan, and the board laid at the bottom of a coffin, the '칠성판', is bored with holes in the shape of the seven stars. It is sometimes shortened to '칠성'.

examples.en: The volcano spewed black smoke.
This fountain shoots water high into the air.
People began to vent the discontent they had held back.
Let out your energy through exercise.
There is a hole that releases gas from underground.

examples.ko: 간헐천은 일정한 시간마다 뜨거운 물을 분출한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a geyser shoots out hot water at regular intervals.

explain: 물·가스·불꽃처럼 안에 있던 것을 세게 밖으로 내뿜을 때 써요. 감정을 풀어낼 때도 '분출하다'를 쓰지만 입말에서는 '터뜨리다'가 더 흔해요. 피동 '분출되다'와 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is used when something inside, such as water, gas or flames, is blown out forcefully. It can also be used for letting emotion out, though 터뜨리다 is more common in speech. It pairs with the passive 분출되다.

examples.en: Rays of light come in through the gap in the window.

examples.ko: 아침 빛살에 눈이 부셔서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The morning light was so bright in my eyes that I woke up.
Rays of light poured down between the leaves.
I rested for a moment in the warm rays of light.
When the clouds cleared, bright rays of light shone down.

examples.ko: 빛살 하나가 책상 위를 비추고 있어요.
examples.en: A single ray of light is shining on the desk.

explain: '햇빛'은 해에서 오는 빛 전체를 말하고, '빛살'은 가늘게 뻗은 줄기 같은 빛을 가리켜요. 해가 만든 빛살은 '햇살'이라고도 하는데, 일상 대화에서는 '햇살'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '햇빛' refers to light from the sun as a whole, while '빛살' points to light stretching out in thin beams. Beams made by the sun are also called '햇살', which sounds more natural in daily conversation.

en: morning star (Venus at dawn); rising star

examples.en: I saw the morning star in the dawn sky for the first time.
I made a wish on that morning star.

examples.ko: 그 신인 선수는 야구계의 샛별로 불려요.
examples.en: That rookie is called a rising star in baseball.

examples.ko: 샛별은 해가 뜨기 직전에 가장 밝아 보여요.
examples.en: The morning star looks brightest just before sunrise.
She was a child who smiled brightly like the morning star.
At dawn the morning star set and the sun came up.

explain: 새벽 동쪽 하늘에 보이는 밝은 별(금성)이에요. 저녁 서쪽 하늘에서 보일 때는 '개밥바라기'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: That singer is a rising star of the K-pop scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 나타나서 앞날이 기대되는 사람에게 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for a newcomer with a promising future.

explain_en: It is the bright star (Venus) seen in the eastern sky at dawn. When it appears in the western sky in the evening, it is called 개밥바라기.

examples.ko: 아침에 밭에 서릿발이 허옇게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: In the morning, white frost spikes were standing in the field.

examples.ko: 서릿발을 밟으니 발밑에서 서걱서걱 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When I stepped on the frost spikes, they crunched under my feet.
Because of frost spikes, the ground heaves in winter.
Everyone froze at the icy-cold look in his eyes.

examples.ko: 선생님의 서릿발 같은 호통에 교실이 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The classroom went quiet at the teacher's stern scolding.

examples.ko: 서릿발에 뿌리가 들려서 보리 싹이 시들었어요.
examples.en: The barley sprouts withered because frost spikes lifted their roots.

explain: '서리'는 얼어붙은 흰 결정을 넓게 말하고, '서릿발'은 땅에서 기둥처럼 솟은 모양에 초점을 둬요. 비유로 차갑고 엄한 기세를 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 서릿발 같은 목소리로 꾸짖어서 아무도 대답하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: He scolded in such a stern voice that nobody could answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기세나 말투가 차갑고 엄해서 두렵게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요. 주로 호통, 눈빛, 명령에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the force or tone is cold and severe enough to feel frightening. It is mainly used for scolding, looks and orders.
phrases.en_equiv: stern as ice; icy and severe

explain_en: '서리' is the frozen white crystals in general, while '서릿발' focuses on the columns standing up from the ground. It is also used figuratively for a cold, stern force.

examples.en: A cold wind is blowing, and the back of my neck feels chilly.
The season has come when the air is chilly morning and evening.
When I stepped on the floor barefoot, my feet felt a cold shock.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣는 순간 가슴이 선뜩했어요.
examples.en: The moment I heard those words, my heart gave a chill.
I felt chilly after my shower, so I put on a jacket.

examples.ko: 가을이 되니 이불 밖이 선뜩하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Now that it's autumn, it feels chilly outside the blanket.

explain: '서늘하다'와 비슷하지만 선뜩하다는 갑자기 차가운 것에 닿거나 차갑게 느껴지는 순간의 느낌이 강해요. 놀라서 가슴이 서늘해지는 느낌에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '서늘하다' (cool), but 선뜩하다 stresses the sudden moment of touching or feeling something cold. It can also describe the chill you feel in your chest when startled.

examples.en: A flash of light streaked across the dark sky.
The camera flash dazzled my eyes.
A good idea suddenly flashed into my mind.
I squeezed my eyes shut at the strong flash.
The dark night sky suddenly lit up with a flash.

examples.ko: 멀리서 섬광을 보고 나서 천둥소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: I saw a flash in the distance and then heard thunder.

explain: 번개나 불빛처럼 아주 짧고 강하게 번쩍이는 빛을 말해요. 일상에서는 '번쩍임', '번개'라고 더 자주 말하고, '섬광'은 글이나 뉴스, 묘사하는 말에서 많이 보여요. '섬광처럼 스치다'는 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때 비유로 써요.
explain_en: It means a very short, strong flash of light like lightning. In everyday talk people more often say '번쩍임' or '번개', while '섬광' appears in writing, news and descriptions. '섬광처럼 스치다' is used figuratively when an idea suddenly comes to mind.

examples.en: The cat takes a nap in a sunny spot.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 양지바른 곳에 앉아 있고 싶어요.
examples.en: In winter, I want to sit in a sunny place.
I hung the laundry out in a sunny spot.
This house gets sun, so it is warm even in winter.
My grandmother dries beans in a sunny spot.
Plants grow better in the sun than in the shade.

explain: '양지'의 반대말은 '음지'로, 햇볕이 드는 곳과 그늘진 곳을 구분할 때 써요. '양지바르다'는 햇빛이 잘 드는 곳을 묘사하는 말이에요. '양지'는 따뜻하고 좋은 곳이라는 느낌이 있어서, 편한 처지를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: The opposite of '양지' is '음지' (shade): sunny spots versus shaded ones. '양지바르다' describes a place that gets plenty of sun. Because '양지' feels warm and good, it can also stand figuratively for a comfortable position.

examples.en: Outside the window, the spring air is already unmistakable.

examples.ko: 그 사람 얼굴에 피곤한 기색이 완연해요.
examples.en: Signs of tiredness are clearly visible on his face.

examples.ko: 산에 가 보니 가을 분위기가 완연한 것 같아요.
examples.en: Going to the mountain, it seems autumn is fully here.

examples.ko: 그의 표정에 긴장한 모습이 완연해서 걱정됐어요.
examples.en: His nervousness showed clearly on his face, so I was worried.
Once spring has fully arrived, let's go on a picnic together.
Joy is plainly written on the child's face.

explain: 계절의 느낌이나 표정, 기색이 눈에 분명히 보일 때 써요. '봄기운이 완연하다', '피곤한 기색이 완연하다'처럼 짝이 되는 말이 있고, 일상 대화보다는 글이나 방송에서 더 자주 들려요. 더 쉬운 말은 '뚜렷하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when a season's feel, an expression or a sign is plainly visible. It has typical partners like '봄기운이 완연하다' and '피곤한 기색이 완연하다', and you hear it more in writing and broadcasts than in casual talk. A simpler word is '뚜렷하다'.

examples.ko: 복도 형광등이 오래돼서 밤이 되면 어둡고 으스스해요.
examples.en: The hallway lights are old, so it's dark and eerie at night.
When the cold wind blew, my body shivered.
I feel chilly, as if I'm catching a cold.

examples.ko: 으스스한 이야기를 들으니 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: After hearing a creepy story, I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 폐가 앞을 지나니 으스스했어요.
examples.en: Passing the abandoned house on a rainy day felt eerie.
I feel a chill in the mornings and evenings.

explain: 몸이 차갑거나 무서워서 소름 끼칠 때 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '으스스 춥다/떨리다'로 쓰고, '으스스하다'로 분위기가 무서울 때도 써요. 감기 기운이 있을 때 쓰는 말로도 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It describes the feeling when you are cold or scared and get goosebumps. It is usually '으스스 춥다/떨리다', and '으스스하다' is used for a creepy atmosphere. It is also natural for the chills you get when coming down with a cold.

examples.en: Tomorrow is Ipdong, so the weather is chilly.
Now that Ipdong has passed, the morning air is cold.
Many households start making kimchi for winter around Ipdong.
This year Ipdong is around November 7.
Around Ipdong, the first ice sometimes forms.
Some homes turn on the heating from Ipdong.

explain: 24절기 중 하나로, 달력에서 겨울이 시작되는 날로 표시돼요. 보통 11월 초이고, 입춘, 입하, 입추처럼 '입-'으로 시작하는 절기 이름과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 날씨 뉴스나 달력에서 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is one of the 24 solar terms and is marked on the calendar as the start of winter, usually in early November. It's good to learn it together with 입춘, 입하 and 입추, the other terms that begin with '입-'. You can see it in weather news and on calendars.

examples.ko: 길 앞에서 개를 보고 잠깐 주춤했어요.
examples.en: I saw a dog in front of me and paused for a moment.

examples.ko: 갑자기 소리가 나서 아이가 주춤하며 뒤를 봤어요.
examples.en: A sudden sound made the child flinch and look back.
The popularity slowed for a while and then rose again.
It was a month when sales slowed because of the rain.

examples.ko: 그는 문 앞에서 주춤해서 들어가지 못했어요.
examples.en: He hesitated at the door and couldn't go in.

examples.ko: 주춤하지 말고 하고 싶은 말을 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't hold back; say what you want to say.

explain: 사람이 놀라거나 망설여서 몸이 잠깐 멈출 때 쓰고, 오르던 숫자나 인기가 잠시 멈출 때도 써요. 완전히 멈추는 게 아니라 잠깐이에요. '망설이다'는 마음이 정해지지 않는 것이고, '주춤하다'는 몸이나 흐름이 잠깐 멈추는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when a person stops for a moment out of surprise or hesitation, and when rising numbers or popularity pause briefly. It is not a full stop, just a short one. 망설이다 is about being undecided in your mind, while 주춤하다 is a body or trend pausing for a moment.

examples.en: I dipped my feet into the ice-cold winter sea.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침 바닥이 차디차서 양말을 두 켤레 신었어요.
examples.en: The floor was freezing on the winter morning, so I wore two pairs of socks.

examples.ko: 손이 차디차네요. 이 장갑을 껴 보세요.
examples.en: Your hands are ice cold. Try putting on these gloves.
That person answered coldly and turned away.
The water is freezing, so get in carefully.

examples.ko: 방이 차디차지 않게 보일러를 켜 두었어요.
examples.en: I left the heating on so the room wouldn't be freezing.

explain: '차다'를 강하게 말한 표현이에요. 말할 때는 '엄청 차다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '차디찬' 모양은 글이나 노래 가사에서 자주 보여요. 사람의 냉정한 태도를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a stronger version of '차다' (cold). In speech people more often say '엄청 차다', while the form '차디찬' appears often in writing and song lyrics. It can also describe a cold, unfeeling attitude.

examples.en: At the zoo, a chimpanzee was eating a banana.
I went to the zoo to see the smart chimpanzees.
I saw a chimpanzee family in a documentary.
The child made everyone laugh by imitating a chimpanzee.
Humans and chimpanzees have a lot in common.
That scholar taught sign language to a chimpanzee.

explain: '원숭이'는 꼬리가 있는 종류를 주로 말하고, 침팬지는 꼬리가 없는 '유인원'이에요. 고릴라, 오랑우탄도 같은 유인원이라서 침팬지와 함께 소개돼요. 사람과 가장 가까운 동물로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 원숭이 mostly refers to tailed monkeys, while 침팬지 is a tailless ape, a 유인원. Gorillas and orangutans are apes too, so they are introduced together with chimpanzees. Chimpanzees often appear as the animal closest to humans.

examples.en: Suddenly raindrops began to patter down.

examples.ko: 비가 그친 뒤 나뭇잎에서 물방울이 후두둑 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, drops pattered down from the leaves.
Hail pelted down on the roof.
When I shook the chestnut tree, chestnuts rained down.

examples.ko: 창문에 후두둑 소리가 나서 밖을 봤어요.
examples.en: I heard a pattering on the window and looked outside.
When I opened the bag, coins spilled out all at once.

explain: 굵은 빗방울, 열매, 작은 물건이 연달아 떨어지는 소리나 모습에 써요. '후두둑 후두둑'처럼 반복해서도 말해요. 후드득과 비슷해서 서로 바꿔 써도 자연스러운 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used for the sound or sight of thick raindrops, fruit or small things falling one after another. You can also repeat it, as in '후두둑 후두둑'. It is close to 후드득, and in many cases you can swap the two naturally.
